title: Does Your Team Need an Elon Musk Moment?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership proposes that teams occasionally need an Elon Musk Moment, a short burst of urgency around a big, bold priority. The argument is that teams fall into comfortable rhythms that breed complacency, and a hot, all-hands priority shakes them loose. The author separates the quality worth borrowing, disrupting the status quo with a bold idea, from any view of Musk himself. Even a priority that turns out to be a dud can restore creative energy. The post warns against overuse and against ideas that are not game-changers, and ends with questions about what would merit such a moment.
points: Teams that settle into the same rhythms need an occasional jolt of urgency to break complacency.
The borrowed lesson is Musk's habit of introducing big, bold ideas and asking everyone to deliver quickly.
Even a priority that fails can shake a team free of monotony and spark creative effort.
Colleagues set aside differences and often do their best work when everyone shares one short-term focus.
The tactic loses force if overused or if the idea is not a real game-changer; it is not a fire drill.
quotes: It’s not that the team is tired or bored. It’s that they get used to the same rhythms and melodies, so the song becomes stale or old.

He introduces big, bold ideas and asks everyone to bring them to fruition in short order. In other words, he disrupts the status quo and injects the organizations he runs with a priority so hot and important that everyone must focus on it, at least for the short-term.
Even if this priority turns out to be a dud, it shakes the team free of the cobwebs of monotony and asks them to find some new creative fuel to execute what has never been done before.
People set aside differences and collaborate to make a short deadline. They feel energized by the urgency of the myopic focus and sometimes do their best work ever.
Doing this too often, or with an idea that is not a game-changer, leaves a bad taste. This is not a fire drill.
When was the last time your team or organization had a singular focus that drew everyone in and engaged the entire team for a few days?
